Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:11:1.hebrew: תא שמע מדד ולא משך לא קנה מאי לאו בסימטא - וקשה לר' אסי. וא"ת: דלמא בכליו של מוכר איירי, ולא הניח על גבי סימטא, ומשום הכי לא קנה. וכי תימא: אי בכליו של מוכר, היכי מהניא משיכה? דודאי מהניא, כמו שאפרש לקמן. ונראה: דמדנקט "מדד ולא משך", משמע דלא מהני מידי אלא משיכה, מדלא קתני "מדד ולא הניח ע"ג קרקע ולא משך":
Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:11:1.english: "Come and hear: If he measured but did not pull, he has not acquired. Is it not [speaking of a case] in an alley?" - And this is difficult for R. Asi. And if you say: Perhaps [the Mishnah] is speaking of [produce] in the seller's vessels, and he did not place it in the alley, and therefore he did not acquire. And if you say: If it is in the seller's vessels, how can pulling be effective? Certainly it is effective, as I will explain below. And it appears that since [the Mishnah] stated "he measured but did not pull," this implies that nothing is effective except pulling, since it did not teach "he measured but did not place it on the ground and did not pull."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:13:1.hebrew: ואי ברה"ר ממאן אגר - אבל בסימטא, מצי אגר מבני ההוא מבוי דפתוח לההוא סימטא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:13:1.english: "And if it is in the public domain, from whom did he rent?" - But in a simta (a side alley), he can rent [the space] from the residents of that dead-end alley that opens onto that simta.

Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:13:2.hebrew: הכי קאמר אי ברשות בעלים היא כו' - כולה ה"מ לאוקמה ברשות בעלים, ולפרש "משך" מרשות בעלים לסימטא; אלא דלא הוה שייך לשון משך, דהוה ליה למימר: הוציאו מרשות בעלים:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:13:2.english: "This is what it is saying: if it is in the owner's domain, etc." - [The Gemara] could have established the entire [Mishnah] as referring to the owner's domain, and explained "pulled" as [pulling] from the owner's domain to the alleyway; but the term "pulled" would not be appropriate, since it should have said: "He removed it from the owner's domain."

Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:1:1.hebrew: יין וחומץ - וא"ת: והא אמר לקמן בהמוכר את הפירות (בבא בתרא דף צו. ושם): הבודק את החבית להיות מפריש עליה תרומה, ואח"כ נמצאת חומץ — כל ג' ימים (הראשונים) ודאי תרומה, מכאן ואילך ספק. פי': שלא תהא תרומתו תרומה. ואמאי? והא לרבנן אמרי' מין אחד הן! וי"ל, דהתם טעמא משום דלא נתכוין להפריש אלא יין, ונמצא חומץ דהוי טעות; אבל נתכוין להפריש חומץ — הוי תרומה. וכן משמע בתוספתא דתרומה (פ"ד). אבל קשה, דאמר בהאשה רבה (יבמות דף פט.): התורם קישות ונמצאת מרה, תרומתו תרומה ויחזור ויתרום; וכן מן הטמא על הטהור, אמר התם דבשוגג תרומתו תרומה אע"פ שטעה. ושם פירשתי:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:1:1.english: Wine and vinegar - And if you ask: But [the Gemara] says later, in [the chapter] "HaMokher et HaPeirot" (Bava Batra 96a, there): One who tests a barrel in order to separate teruma [tithe] from it, and afterward it is found to be vinegar — for all of the [first] three days, it is certainly teruma; from then on, it is uncertain. Meaning, [it is uncertain] whether his teruma is [valid] teruma. But why [is it uncertain]? Don't we say, according to the Rabbis, that [wine and vinegar] are one species?! And one can answer: There the reason is that he intended to separate only wine, and it was found to be vinegar, which is a mistake. But if he intended to separate vinegar, it is [valid] teruma. And so it implies in the Tosefta of Teruma (chapter 4). But it is difficult, for [the Gemara] says in [the chapter] "HaIshah Rabbah" (Yevamot 89a): One who separates teruma from cucumbers and they are found to be bitter, his teruma is [valid] teruma, and he must go back and separate teruma again; and likewise [one who separates] from the impure for the pure — [the Gemara] says there that if done unintentionally, his teruma is [valid] teruma even though he erred. And there I have explained:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:5:1.hebrew: מדד והניח ע"ג סימטא קנה - כשהמוכר מודד איירי. אע"פ שמשיכת המוכר אינה מועלת ללוקח, הכא שאני, כשמודד ומניח על גבי סימטא. אבל מדד לוקח — פשיטא! ובהא לא הוה ס"ד, דא"ר זירא: שמא לא שמע רבי אלא במודד לתוך קופתו, אבל על גבי קרקע לא. אע"ג דמשיכה מועלת בסימטא, כאילו מושך ברשותו; בלא משיכה מיהא לא קנה בסימטא:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:5:1.english: "He measured and placed [the produce] on the ground in an alleyway, he has acquired [it]" - [The Gemara] is speaking of when the seller measures. Even though the seller's pulling is not effective for the buyer, here it is different, when he measures and places [the produce] on the ground in an alleyway. But if the buyer measured, it is obvious [that he acquires]. And about this [case of the seller measuring] it would not have entered one's mind [that he acquires], for R. Zeira said: Perhaps Rabbi heard [this ruling] only where [the seller] measures into [the buyer's] basket, but [where he measures] onto the ground, no. Even though pulling is effective in an alleyway, as if he were pulling in his own domain, without pulling, at any rate, he has not acquired in an alleyway:

Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:9:1.hebrew: חצר השותפין קונין זה מזה - משמע מתוך הלשון שהחצר קונה בלא זכיית כליו, ומשמע ליה דקנה אף בלא משיכה:
Tosafot on Bava Batra 84b:9:1.english: "A courtyard of partners, they acquire from one another" - It is implied from the wording that the courtyard acquires without the acquisition [being effected] through his vessels, and [the questioner] understood from it that he acquired even without pulling (meshikhah).
